mainTopic: Does an אומן own the שבח he adds to an item? רב אסי's rule tested against the dyer משנה, בל תלין, and the betrothal-with-jewelry ברייתא
overview: Just before this, רב אסי ruled that an אומן קונה בשבח כלי: a craftsman gets ownership rights in the added value he puts into an item. The גמרא first tries to prove this from the משנה about a dyer whose cauldron burned the wool. שמואל pushes the proof away, and the גמרא concludes he was only deflecting it, not arguing with רב אסי. Next the גמרא tries a ברייתא that applies בל תלין to a craftsman's pay. It answers that the ברייתא is about a worker paid per tread, who is a plain hired worker. Along the way, the גמרא shows that רב ששת's ruling on a contractor fits with רב אסי, because רב ששת means a letter carrier who improves nothing. Finally, the גמרא asks whether רבי מאיר and the חכמים argue about רב אסי's rule in a case of betrothal with jewelry. It gives two other explanations of their argument, one about when a wage is owed and one about betrothing with a loan. So the ברייתא does not prove that the rule is argued about by תנאים.

steps.title: Trying to prove רב אסי's rule from the burned-wool משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: if the dyer's cauldron burned the wool, he pays only the value of the wool. It reads this as a case where the dye already improved the wool, which would mean the אומן owns the improvement.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: if the cauldron burned the wool, the dyer gives the owner the value of his wool. The value of the wool, yes; the value of the wool plus the improvement, no. Isn't this a case where it burned after it fell in, when there already was an improvement? So we learn that a craftsman acquires the improvement of an item.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה and points out a detail: the dyer pays only for the plain wool, not for the improvement. It uses that detail to try to prove רב אסי's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the dye had already taken hold, the wool was worth more before it burned. If the dyer does not have to pay for that extra value, it must be because the extra value counts as his. That is exactly רב אסי's rule, אומן קונה בשבח כלי.

keyTerms.meaning: a craftsman acquires the improvement he puts into an item (רב אסי's rule)
and learn from it, a formula that draws a proof

steps.confusionAlert: The dyer is not getting the wool itself. The question is only who owns the extra value the dye added.

phrases.english: and the cauldron burned it –
phrases.notes: This is a quote from the משנה about someone who gave wool to a dyer.

phrases.english: he gives him the value of his wool.
The value of his wool – yes,
the value of his wool and its improvement – no;
is it not that it burned after it fell in,
when there is an improvement,
and learn from it
that a craftsman acquires the improvement of an item?

steps.triggerLanguage: לָאו שֶׁהִקְדִּיחוֹ לְאַחַר נְפִילָה, דְּאִיכָּא שְׁבָחָא, וּשְׁמַע מִינַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the attempt to support רב אסי's earlier rule.
steps.raayaObject: רב אסי's rule: אומן קונה בשבח כלי
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's wording 'דמי צמרו', which leaves out the improvement

steps.title: שמואל: the wool burned right away, before any improvement
steps.stepSummary: שמואל rejects the proof. The משנה is talking about wool that burned the moment it fell in, so there was never any improvement to pay for.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: What case are we dealing with here? Where it burned at the moment it fell in, so there is no improvement.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל blocks the proof by setting the משנה in a different case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the wool burned immediately, the dye never took hold. So the dyer pays only for plain wool simply because that is all the wool was ever worth. The משנה then says nothing about who owns an improvement.

keyTerms.meaning: what case are we dealing with here? (used to narrow a source to a specific case)
at the moment of falling in

phrases.english: שמואל said: What case are we dealing with here?
For example, where it burned at the moment it fell in,
so there is no improvement.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from step 1.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof from the משנה, not רב אסי's rule itself
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the dye had already taken hold, but the משנה can be about wool that burned instantly.

steps.title: Does שמואל disagree with רב אסי?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what שמואל would say if the wool burned after the dye took hold. Would the dyer pay for the improvement too? That would mean שמואל rejects רב אסי's rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if it burned after it fell in, what then? He gives him the value of his wool and its improvement?! Shall we say שמואל does not hold like רב אסי?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא presses שמואל. His answer seems to suggest he disagrees with רב אסי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By saying the משנה is only about wool that burned instantly, שמואל implies that later on things would be different. Then the dyer would have to pay for the improvement, which means the אומן does not own it. That goes against רב אסי.

keyTerms.meaning: shall we say? (offers a possible conclusion)
he does not hold of / does not accept

phrases.english: But if it burned after it fell in, what then?
He gives him the value of his wool and its improvement?!

phrases.aramaic: לֵימָא שְׁמוּאֵל לֵית לֵיהּ דְּרַב אַסִּי?
phrases.english: Shall we say שמואל does not hold like רב אסי?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an uncomfortable implication from שמואל's answer in step 2.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the משנה must be about instant burning, then later burning would require paying for the improvement. That contradicts רב אסי.

steps.title: Another reading: the owner supplied both the wool and the dyes
steps.stepSummary: שמואל could answer that the משנה is talking about a case where the wool and the dyes both belong to the owner, and the dyer only takes a wage for his work. In that case the dyer does not own the improvement.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל could tell you: What case are we dealing with here? Where the wool and the dyes belong to the owner, and the dyer takes only the wage for his work.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that שמואל does not have to disagree with רב אסי. It offers another way to read the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אסי's rule fits a craftsman who adds his own materials. When the owner supplied everything and the dyer only earns a wage, the improvement is not his. So the משנה can be about burning after the dye took hold and still not argue with רב אסי.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לָךְ שְׁמוּאֵל: הָכָא בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן –
phrases.english: שמואל could tell you: What case are we dealing with here?
For example, where the wool and the dyes belong to the owner,
and the dyer takes only the wage for his work.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָךְ שְׁמוּאֵל: הָכָא בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Places the משנה in a different case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שמואל must reject רב אסי's rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is about a dyer working only for a wage, where רב אסי's rule does not apply.

steps.title: Then the משנה should have mentioned the dyes too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: if the dyes also belonged to the owner and were ruined, the משנה should have said the dyer pays for the wool and the dyes.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, it should have said: 'He gives him the value of his wool and dyes!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the new reading by pointing to the משנה's exact wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the owner's dyes were lost in the burning, the dyer should owe for them as well. The משנה mentions only the wool, so this reading does not fit its words.

phrases.english: If so,

phrases.aramaic: ״נוֹתֵן לוֹ דְּמֵי צַמְרוֹ וְסַמָּנִין״ מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ!
phrases.english: it should have said: 'He gives him the value of his wool and dyes!'

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, נוֹתֵן לוֹ דְּמֵי צַמְרוֹ וְסַמָּנִין מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading offered in step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that the owner supplied both wool and dyes
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה's wording mentions payment for wool only, not for dyes.

steps.title: שמואל was only pushing off the proof
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that שמואל was only deflecting the proof for רב אסי. He was not stating his own opinion against רב אסי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, שמואל was only pushing off the proof.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the attempt to explain שמואל through step 4. It concludes that his answer in step 2 was just a way to deflect the proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל's case of instant burning was meant only to show that the משנה is not a proof. It does not mean he actually holds that a dyer pays for the improvement. So we cannot conclude that שמואל argues with רב אסי.

keyTerms.meaning: he is merely pushing it off, deflecting a proof without stating his own view

steps.whatToRemember: The proof for רב אסי from the burned-wool משנה fails, because the משנה can be about wool that burned instantly. But שמואל's answer was only a deflection. It does not show he disagrees with רב אסי.

phrases.english: Rather, שמואל
was only pushing it off.
phrases.notes: He was just knocking down the proof, not saying what he himself holds.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא שְׁמוּאֵל דַּחוֹיֵי קָא מְדַחֵי לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives up on step 4's reading and resolves step 3's challenge differently.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: שמואל only deflected the proof; there is no evidence that he rejects רב אסי's rule.

steps.title: A new proof from the garment given to a craftsman
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא. A craftsman who finished a garment but has not returned it can wait ten days for pay without the owner violating בל תלין. If he returned it at midday, the owner violates בל תלין once the sun sets.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: Someone gives his garment to a craftsman. If the craftsman finished it and told him so, the owner does not violate 'do not keep wages overnight' even if ten days pass. But if the craftsman handed the garment back at midday, then once the sun sets the owner does violate 'do not keep wages overnight.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא as a possible proof on whether a craftsman owns the improvement. This step only quotes the source; the next step explains how it proves anything.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא treats the craftsman's pay as a wage that falls under בל תלין once the garment is handed back. That detail will be used in the next step as evidence about who owns the improvement.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear: the גמרא is bringing a source as a proof
A craftsman who works on someone else's item
The prohibition against holding back a worker's wages overnight

phrases.english: Come and hear:
One who gives his garment to a craftsman;
he finished it and notified him —
even from now until ten days
he does not transgress over it because of 'do not keep overnight.'
If he gave it to him at midday —
once the sun has set on him,
he transgresses over it because of 'do not keep overnight.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the proof from the dyer was set aside, the גמרא tries a new source on the same question.
steps.raayaObject: That a craftsman does not acquire ownership of the improvement he adds (אומן אינו קונה בשבח כלי).
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא applying בל תלין to a craftsman's pay once the garment is returned.

steps.title: If the craftsman owned the improvement, there would be no wage to delay
steps.stepSummary: If a craftsman owns the improvement, the payment is a purchase, not a wage. Then why would the owner violate בל תלין?
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you think a craftsman acquires the improvement of the item, why does the owner violate 'do not keep wages overnight'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws the proof out of the ברייתא. If the craftsman owned the improvement, the owner would be buying it, and בל תלין would not apply.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בל תלין applies only to wages, meaning pay for work. If the craftsman owned the improvement, the money would be a sale price, and a late sale price is not a delayed wage. Since the ברייתא does apply בל תלין, it seems the craftsman does not own the improvement.

keyTerms.meaning: And if it enters your mind: introduces an idea in order to challenge it
A craftsman acquires the improvement he made to the item

phrases.english: And if it enters your mind
that a craftsman acquires through the improvement of the item,
why does he transgress because of 'do not keep overnight'?
phrases.notes: Late payment for something you bought is not a delayed wage. That is the whole point of the question.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ אוּמָּן קוֹנֶה בִּשְׁבַח כְּלִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the quoted ברייתא into a challenge against the view that the craftsman owns the improvement.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that אומן קונה בשבח כלי, which is רב אסי's own rule.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: בל תלין applies only to wages. If the craftsman owned the improvement, the payment would be a purchase, so בל תלין should not apply. The ברייתא says it does apply.

steps.title: The garment in the ברייתא gets no real improvement
steps.stepSummary: רב מרי בריה דרב כהנא says the ברייתא is about laundering a thick, coarse garment. That work adds no improvement, so there is nothing for the craftsman to own.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מרי, son of רב כהנא, said: The ברייתא is talking about laundering a thick, coarse garment, where there is no improvement.
steps.whatsHappening: רב מרי defends the view that a craftsman owns the improvement. He says the ברייתא is a case with no improvement at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule 'a craftsman owns the improvement' only matters when there is an improvement. If the work adds nothing, the pay can only be a wage, and בל תלין applies. So the ברייתא does not argue against that rule.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב מָרִי בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב כָּהֲנָא:
phrases.english: Rav Mari, son of Rav Kahana, said:
With the laundering of a coarse garment,
phrases.notes: Washing a rough, heavy cloak doesn't really make it worth more.

phrases.english: where there is no improvement.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב מָרִי בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב כָּהֲנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by narrowing the ברייתא's case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to be about any work on a garment, including work that adds value.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is about work that adds no value, so the pay is only a wage.

steps.title: Softening the garment is itself an improvement
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: the owner gave the garment in order to soften it. Once it is softened, that is an improvement.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the end, why did he give it to him? To soften it. Once he softened it, that is an improvement!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב מרי's answer. Even a coarse garment comes back softer, and that is exactly the improvement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No one hands over a garment for work that does nothing. Softening is the purpose of the work, so there is an improvement after all. The original question from בל תלין comes back.

keyTerms.meaning: In the end, ultimately: pushing back against an answer
That is, this is the same as

phrases.english: In the end,
for what did he give it to him? To soften it;
once he has softened it, that is an improvement!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב מרי's claim that there is no improvement.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב מרי's answer that laundering a coarse garment adds no improvement.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The whole purpose of the work is softening, and softening is an improvement. So the craftsman would own it, and the question from בל תלין returns.

steps.title: He was paid per tread, so he is a plain hired worker
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the craftsman was hired to tread on the garment for a מעה per tread. Being paid per action makes him a hired worker, so בל תלין applies.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, the ברייתא is needed for a case where the owner hired him for treads, a מעה for each tread. That is hired labor.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new case for the ברייתא. The craftsman is paid for each tread he does, not for the finished result.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When a worker is paid per action, the money is for his effort, not for the result on the garment. So even if the garment gets softer, the pay is a wage and falls under בל תלין. The ברייתא no longer disproves the view that a craftsman owns the improvement in a regular job.

keyTerms.meaning: It is only needed for: introduces the specific case the source is talking about
A tread: stamping on the cloth in water to soften it
Hired labor, paid for the work itself

steps.whatToRemember: The proof from בל תלין is set aside. The ברייתא is about a worker paid per tread, which is a wage, so it tells us nothing about a craftsman paid for a finished job.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the garment gets no improvement here. It does get softer. The point is that the pay is counted per tread, so it is a wage for effort and not a price for the result.

phrases.english: No, it is needed
where he hired him for treads —
phrases.notes: Treading means stamping on the wet cloth with your feet to soften it.

phrases.english: each tread for a ma'ah,
which is hired labor.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection that softening is an improvement by changing how the worker is paid.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case (אוקימתא) by the payment arrangement
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any work that improves the garment makes the craftsman an owner of the improvement, so his pay would not be a wage.
steps.terutzMaskana: A worker paid per tread is a hired laborer paid for effort, so his pay is a wage under בל תלין whatever the result.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that how a worker is paid, per action or per finished job, can decide whether his pay counts as a wage for בל תלין.

steps.title: The original reading would have supported רב ששת
steps.stepSummary: Before the answer in Step 11, we assumed the worker was not hired per tread. On that reading, the ברייתא supports רב ששת, who ruled that a contractor's employer violates בל תלין.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to what we first thought, that he was not hired per tread, the ברייתא supports רב ששת. They asked רב ששת: if someone hires a contractor, does he violate בל תלין or not? רב ששת told them: he violates it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא looks back at its first understanding of the ברייתא and points out that it would have backed up a ruling of רב ששת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At first we thought the craftsman was paid for the finished job, like a contractor, and the ברייתא still said בל תלין applies. רב ששת says the same thing about a contractor, so that first reading supports him. This sets up the next question: how does רב ששת fit with רב אסי?

keyTerms.meaning: Contract work: paid for the finished job, not by the hour or day
The prohibition against holding back a worker's wages overnight
Treadings: stepping on a garment to clean or soften it

phrases.english: And according to what entered our minds at first
that he did not hire him for treadings,
phrases.notes: This is how we read the ברייתא before Step 11 said he was paid per tread.

phrases.english: it supports Rav Sheshet –
for they asked Rav Sheshet:
A contractor: does one violate on account of him the prohibition of 'do not delay [wages]',
or does one not violate it?
And Rav Sheshet said to them: He violates it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Looks back at the reading the גמרא used before Step 11 and shows it would have supported רב ששת.
steps.raayaObject: רב ששת's ruling that hiring a contractor is covered by בל תלין
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא about the craftsman (Step 7), read the way we first understood it (not paid per tread)

steps.title: Does רב ששת argue with רב אסי?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether רב ששת's ruling contradicts רב אסי, who holds that a craftsman owns his improvement.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say that רב ששת disagrees with רב אסי?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a problem: רב ששת's ruling seems to clash with רב אסי's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אסי says a craftsman owns the improvement he makes, so his pay counts as a purchase and not a wage. Then בל תלין should not apply to a contractor. Yet רב ששת says it does apply, so the two seem to disagree.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say? (a suggestion the גמרא tests)

phrases.aramaic: לֵימָא דְּרַב שֵׁשֶׁת פְּלִיגָא אַדְּרַב אַסִּי?
phrases.english: Shall we say that Rav Sheshet disagrees with Rav Asi?
phrases.notes: רב אסי is the one who said a craftsman owns the improvement he makes to the item.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵימָא דְּרַב שֵׁשֶׁת פְּלִיגָא אַדְּרַב אַסִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the ruling of רב ששת quoted in Step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב ששת's ruling that a contractor is covered by בל תלין
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a craftsman owns his improvement (רב אסי), his pay is a purchase price and not a wage, so בל תלין should not apply.

steps.title: רב ששת means someone delivering a letter
steps.stepSummary: שמואל בר אחא answers that רב ששת's contractor is a messenger hired to deliver a letter. He improves nothing, so there is nothing for him to own.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל בר אחא said: רב ששת is talking about a letter carrier.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל בר אחא resolves the clash by narrowing the kind of contractor רב ששת meant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A letter carrier is paid per job, but he does not improve any object. רב אסי's ownership idea can't apply to him, so his pay is a real wage and בל תלין applies. That means רב ששת and רב אסי don't disagree.
steps.whatToRemember: A contractor who improves an item may own the improvement (רב אסי). A contractor who improves nothing, like a letter carrier, is a regular worker, and בל תלין applies (רב ששת).

phrases.english: Shmuel bar Aḥa said:
[He is speaking] of a messenger carrying a letter.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר אַחָא: בִּשְׁלִיחָא דְאִיגַּרְתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 13.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב ששת meant any contractor, even one who improves an item, which would clash with רב אסי.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב ששת meant a contractor who improves nothing, like a letter carrier, so there is no clash.

steps.title: Suggesting that רב אסי's idea is a dispute of תנאים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that רב אסי's rule may be the subject of a dispute between תנאים. It quotes a ברייתא about betrothal through jewelry the man makes.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say this is like a dispute of תנאים? A woman says, 'Make me bracelets, earrings and rings, and I will be betrothed to you.' Once he makes them, she is betrothed; this is רבי מאיר's view. The חכמים say she is not betrothed until money reaches her hand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to test whether רב אסי's idea depends on a disagreement between רבי מאיר and the חכמים. This sets up the analysis that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A woman asks a goldsmith to make jewelry and offers to be betrothed as payment. רבי מאיר says she is betrothed once the jewelry is made. The חכמים say she is not betrothed until money reaches her. The next steps work out what 'money' means here.

phrases.english: Shall we say it is like a dispute of Tannaim?
'Make for me bracelets, earrings and rings,'
phrases.notes: The woman is saying this to a goldsmith, using her own gold.

phrases.english: 'and I will be betrothed to you',
once he has made them – she is betrothed,
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.
And the Rabbis say: She is not betrothed
until money reaches her hand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After settling רב ששת, the גמרא looks for a תנאים dispute about רב אסי's rule.
steps.raayaObject: רב אסי's rule that a craftsman owns his improvement
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא on betrothal through jewelry the man makes (רבי מאיר and the חכמים)

steps.title: What does 'money' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the חכמים mean by the 'money' that must reach her hand.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the 'money'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question about a single word in the ברייתא. It is setting up two possible answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everything depends on which 'money' the חכמים require. Is it the jewelry itself, or some other money? The גמרא will test each option.

phrases.english: What is 'money'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about a word in the ברייתא quoted in Step 15.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which money the חכמים require for the betrothal to take effect

steps.title: It can't mean the jewelry itself
steps.stepSummary: If 'money' meant the jewelry itself, then רבי מאיר would hold she is betrothed without even getting the jewelry. With what would she be betrothed? So this reading fails.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it means that same money, it would follow that רבי מאיר holds she doesn't need even that money. Then with what is she betrothed?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the first possible meaning of 'money' and rejects it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the חכמים only require the jewelry to reach her, then רבי מאיר, who argues, would not require even that. But a betrothal needs something of value to be given. Without the jewelry, nothing at all is given, which makes no sense.

phrases.english: If you say it is that same money,
phrases.notes: He means the jewelry he made for her.

phrases.english: it follows that Rabbi Meir holds
that even that money is not [needed]?!
But then with what is she betrothed?
phrases.notes: Some versions have the extra letters in square brackets. They don't change the meaning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries out the first answer to Step 16's question and rejects it.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The reading that 'money' means the jewelry itself
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It would leave רבי מאיר with a betrothal where nothing at all is given to the woman.

steps.title: It must mean other money
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that the 'money' the חכמים require must be other money, beyond the jewelry.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is obvious: what is 'money'? Other money.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the answer to Step 16: the חכמים mean some other money. The ברייתא's link to רב אסי's rule is still being built here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the jewelry can't be what the חכמים mean, they must require something more to reach her hand. So the dispute is whether the jewelry alone is enough (רבי מאיר) or other money is needed (חכמים).

phrases.english: Rather, it is obvious,
what is 'money'? – other money;

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting the first meaning in Step 17, gives the meaning that works.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The חכמים require other money beyond the jewelry. רבי מאיר holds the jewelry itself is enough.

steps.title: Two assumptions behind the proof
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא states two points that everyone is assumed to agree on: a wage builds up from the beginning of the job to the end, and betrothing with a loan does not work.
steps.simpleTranslation: The people who wanted to prove this assumed two things. First, everyone agrees that a worker's wage is owed bit by bit, from the start of the job until the end. Second, everyone agrees that if a man betroths a woman with a loan, she is not betrothed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. It lists two assumptions that will make the proof in the next step work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the wage builds up from the start, then by the time the jewelry is finished, the woman already owes the goldsmith his pay as a debt. Letting her off that debt is like betrothing with a loan, which does not work. So the wage alone cannot explain why רבי מאיר says she is betrothed.

keyTerms.meaning: They assumed it (the people trying to make the proof)
From the beginning until the end (the wage builds up all along)
One who betroths a woman by letting her off a loan she owes him

phrases.english: And they assumed that everyone agrees
that a wage is owed from the beginning until the end;
phrases.notes: He means the worker's pay piles up little by little as he works, so it is already a debt while he is working.

phrases.english: and that everyone agrees
one who betroths with a loan,
she is not betrothed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on step 18's conclusion that the חכמים require extra money. It adds the background assumptions needed to turn the ברייתא into a proof.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Assumed by all: a wage builds up from start to finish, so it becomes a loan, and betrothal with a loan is not valid.

steps.title: So the dispute must be about the craftsman owning the improvement
steps.stepSummary: Given the two assumptions, the גמרא suggests that רבי מאיר holds a craftsman owns the improvement of the vessel, and the חכמים hold he does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't it true that they argue about whether a craftsman owns the improvement he made to a vessel? רבי מאיר holds that he does own it, and the חכמים hold that he does not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now uses the two assumptions to suggest a reason for the argument in the ברייתא. It ties the argument to the rule אומן קונה בשבח כלי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The wage cannot be what betroths her, since it is a loan. So according to רבי מאיר, what does she receive? It must be the goldsmith's own share, the added value of the jewelry, which he owns. The חכמים say he owns nothing in it, so she needs other money.

keyTerms.meaning: What, is it not...? (a lead-in to a suggested explanation)
Acquires (owns) the added value of the vessel he improved

steps.whyThisMatters: If this were right, the rule that a craftsman owns the improvement would turn out to be an argument between תנאים.

phrases.english: What, is it not
about whether a craftsman acquires the improvement of a vessel that they disagree?
For רבי מאיר holds:
a craftsman acquires the improvement of a vessel,
and the Rabbis hold:
a craftsman does not acquire the improvement of a vessel?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי, לָאו בְּאוּמָּן קוֹנֶה בִּשְׁבַח כְּלִי קָמִיפַּלְגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion that the assumptions of step 19 point to.
steps.raayaObject: That the rule אומן קונה בשבח כלי is argued about by תנאים
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא about betrothal with jewelry the man made, read together with the two assumptions

steps.title: No, they argue about when a wage is owed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. Everyone may agree the craftsman does not own the improvement. The real argument is about whether a wage builds up from the beginning.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. Everyone agrees that a craftsman does not own the improvement of a vessel. Here they argue about whether a wage is owed bit by bit from the beginning until the end.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof. It says the argument in the ברייתא can be explained another way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof depended on everyone agreeing that a wage builds up from the start. The גמרא now says that very point is the argument. Once that assumption falls, nobody needs the rule that a craftsman owns the improvement.

phrases.english: No, everyone agrees that
a craftsman does not acquire the improvement of a vessel;
rather, here

phrases.aramaic: בְּיֶשְׁנָהּ לִשְׂכִירוּת מִתְּחִילָּה וְעַד סוֹף קָא מִיפַּלְגִי –
phrases.english: they disagree about whether a wage is owed from the beginning until the end.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא אֵין אוּמָּן קוֹנֶה בִּשְׁבַח כְּלִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects step 20's proof by denying one of step 19's assumptions.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof that אומן קונה בשבח כלי is argued about by תנאים
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof wrongly assumed that everyone agrees a wage builds up from the beginning. That point itself may be the argument.

steps.title: Each side's view on when the wage is owed
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר holds a wage is owed only at the end of the job. The חכמים hold it builds up from the beginning until the end.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר holds that a wage is owed only at the end. The חכמים hold that a wage is owed from the beginning until the end.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out the new explanation, showing what each side holds about wages.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי מאיר, the pay first becomes owed when he hands over the finished jewelry. So it was never a loan, and letting her keep that pay is like giving her fresh money, which betroths her. For the חכמים, the pay was a debt all along, so it is betrothal with a loan and she needs other money.

keyTerms.meaning: At the end (the wage is owed only when the job is finished)
The חכמים, the Rabbis who argue with רבי מאיר

steps.confusionAlert: Don't get mixed up: רבי מאיר's view that the wage is owed 'only at the end' is what makes the betrothal work. Since the pay was never a debt, it is not a loan.
steps.whatToRemember: The argument in the ברייתא may not be about the craftsman owning the improvement at all. It can be explained as an argument about when a wage becomes owed. So it does not prove that the rule is argued about by תנאים.

phrases.english: רבי מאיר holds:
a wage is owed only at the end,
and the Rabbis hold:
a wage is owed from the beginning until the end.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי מֵאִיר סָבַר: אֵין לִשְׂכִירוּת אֶלָּא לְבַסּוֹף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Fills in the details of the other explanation given in step 21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reframing the argument around a different issue
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The argument must be about whether the craftsman owns the improvement of the vessel.
steps.terutzMaskana: The argument can be about when a wage is owed. רבי מאיר says only at the end, so it is not a loan. The חכמים say from the beginning, so it is a loan.

steps.title: A second explanation: the argument is about betrothing with a loan
steps.stepSummary: Everyone agrees a wage builds up from the beginning of the job. The argument is about betrothing with a loan: רבי מאיר says it works, and the חכמים say it does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or, if you want, you can explain it differently. Everyone agrees that a wage builds up from the beginning of the job until the end. Here they argue about someone who betroths a woman with a loan. רבי מאיר holds that if someone betroths with a loan, she is betrothed. The חכמים hold that if someone betroths with a loan, she is not betrothed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second, different explanation of what רבי מאיר and the חכמים are arguing about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 22, the argument was about when a wage is owed, while everyone agreed a loan cannot be used for betrothal. Now the גמרא flips this. Everyone agrees the wage builds up from the start, so by the end it has become a debt, which is like a loan. The argument is only whether betrothing with a loan works.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you want, say instead: introduces a second, alternative answer
A wage builds up from the beginning of the job to the end
One who betroths a woman with a loan, using a debt as the betrothal money
She is betrothed; the קידושין takes effect

steps.whatToRemember: There are two ways to understand the argument. (1) Everyone agrees a loan cannot be used for betrothal, and they argue about when a wage is owed. (2) Everyone agrees a wage builds up from the start, and they argue about whether a loan can be used for betrothal. Neither explanation needs the idea that a craftsman owns the improvement, so the ברייתא does not prove that אומן קונה בשבח כלי is argued about by תנאים.
steps.confusionAlert: Step 19 said everyone agrees betrothing with a loan does not work. This answer drops that assumption on purpose. It is a separate, alternative explanation, not a contradiction.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the case does not prove anything about whether a craftsman owns the improvement. The argument can be explained without that idea at all.

phrases.english: And if you want, say:
that everyone agrees a wage builds up
from the beginning until the end,
phrases.notes: So by the time the job is done, the wage owed is already a debt, just like a loan.

phrases.english: and here they argue about one who betroths with a loan –
for רבי מאיר holds:
one who betroths with a loan – she is betrothed,
and the Rabbis hold:
one who betroths with a loan – she is not betrothed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second explanation, different from step 22, of why רבי מאיר and the חכמים argue, again without needing the idea that a craftsman owns the improvement.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Relocating the argument: switches which of the two assumptions is agreed upon and which is disputed.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The argument had to be about the craftsman owning the improvement, or, as in step 22, about when a wage is owed.
steps.terutzMaskana: Everyone agrees a wage builds up from the start, so it becomes a loan. They argue only about whether a loan can be used for betrothal: רבי מאיר says yes, the חכמים say no.
